Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

content.text:
Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/

response.answer:
### Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering — short overview

This is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor’s Degree** program at the **Burnaby campus**, delivered in person through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- The first two years provide a broad, practical foundation in civil engineering.
- Students receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two academic years.
- The final two years focus on advanced engineering theory, design, project work, management, and a team-based capstone project.
- Coursework includes areas such as surveying, materials, structures, geotechnical engineering, transportation, water resources, mathematics, and communication.
- Optional co-op work terms are available in the program course list.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
program.school: School of Construction and the Environment

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

### Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering — short overview

This is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor’s Degree** program at the **Burnaby campus**, delivered in person through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- The first two years provide a broad, practical foundation in civil engineering.
- Students receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two academic years.
- The final two years focus on advanced engineering theory, design, project work, management, and a team-based capstone project.
- Coursework includes areas such as surveying, materials, structures, geotechnical engineering, transportation, water resources, mathematics, and communication.
- Optional co-op work terms are available in the program course list.

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

conversation.content: I'm exploring Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering. Please keep that as our subject.

Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/
Give me a short overview.

### Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering — short overview

This is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor’s Degree** program at the **Burnaby campus**, delivered in person through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- The first two years provide a broad, practical foundation in civil engineering.
- Students receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two academic years.
- The final two years focus on advanced engineering theory, design, project work, management, and a team-based capstone project.
- Coursework includes areas such as surveying, materials, structures, geotechnical engineering, transportation, water resources, mathematics, and communication.
- Optional co-op work terms are available in the program course list.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor’s Degree**: the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** credential.

You also receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two years of academic study. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
Where would I study?

You would study at the **Burnaby campus**, in person, through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
program.school: School of Construction and the Environment

conversation.content: I'm exploring Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering. Please keep that as our subject.

Understood—I’ll keep **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** as our subject.

### Program overview
- **Credential:** Bachelor’s Degree  
- **Study mode:** Full-time  
- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **School:** School of Construction and the Environment  
- **Length:** Four years of full-time academic study  
- **Status:** Active  

The first two years provide a broad practical foundation in civil engineering. Successful completion of those first two years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** within the degree pathway. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed to the final two years, which include advanced engineering theory, design, project work, and a team-based capstone project.

### Related courses
The program’s course list covers Levels 1–8. Examples include:

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**
- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**

The full program course list includes core courses, technical electives, Liberal Studies electives, and optional co-op work terms.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/
Give me a short overview.

### Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering — short overview

This is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor’s Degree** program at the **Burnaby campus**, delivered in person through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- The first two years provide a broad, practical foundation in civil engineering.
- Students receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two academic years.
- The final two years focus on advanced engineering theory, design, project work, management, and a team-based capstone project.
- Coursework includes areas such as surveying, materials, structures, geotechnical engineering, transportation, water resources, mathematics, and communication.
- Optional co-op work terms are available in the program course list.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor’s Degree**: the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** credential.

Where would I study?

You would study at the **Burnaby campus**, in person, through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at the **Burnaby campus**. The program is full-time.

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

conversation.content: Give me a short overview.

### Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering — short overview

This is a **four-year, full-time Bachelor’s Degree** program at the **Burnaby campus**, delivered in person through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- The first two years provide a broad, practical foundation in civil engineering.
- Students receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two academic years.
- The final two years focus on advanced engineering theory, design, project work, management, and a team-based capstone project.
- Coursework includes areas such as surveying, materials, structures, geotechnical engineering, transportation, water resources, mathematics, and communication.
- Optional co-op work terms are available in the program course list.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor’s Degree**: the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** credential.

You also receive a **Diploma in Civil Engineering** after successfully completing the first two years of academic study. [Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
Where would I study?

You would study at the **Burnaby campus**, in person, through the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
Is it online or in person?

It is **in person** at the **Burnaby campus**. The program is full-time.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
Is it full-time or part-time?

It is **full-time**. The Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering consists of **four years of full-time academic study**.

[Program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

response.answer:
Before applying to the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering**, know that admission is **competitive**. The stored minimum requirements are:

### Minimum academic requirements
- High-school graduation
- **English Studies 12** or equivalent: **73%**
- **Pre-Calculus 12** or an accepted BC/Yukon equivalent: **73%**
- **Chemistry 11**: **73%**
- **Physics 12**: **73%**
- One approved Grade 12 academic course: **73%**  
  *The approved-course equivalency requires institutional confirmation.*

### Application and selection
- Submit the **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**.
- The program area ranks qualified applicants based on **academic success, recency, and complete records**. This ranking is an institutional decision and cannot be determined from the available data.

If you are applying as an international student, the available record indicates the program is available for international eligibility review, but **study-permit information is not published in the available data**.

[View the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

Before applying to the **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering**, know that admission is **competitive**. The stored minimum requirements are:

### Minimum academic requirements
- High-school graduation
- **English Studies 12** or equivalent: **73%**
- **Pre-Calculus 12** or an accepted BC/Yukon equivalent: **73%**
- **Chemistry 11**: **73%**
- **Physics 12**: **73%**
- One approved Grade 12 academic course: **73%**  
  *The approved-course equivalency requires institutional confirmation.*

### Application and selection
- Submit the **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**.
- The program area ranks qualified applicants based on **academic success, recency, and complete records**. This ranking is an institutional decision and cannot be determined from the available data.

If you are applying as an international student, the available record indicates the program is available for international eligibility review, but **study-permit information is not published in the available data**.

[View the program details and application information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

program.program_overview: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.

If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Be concise and clear. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. content.text:
For **international applicants**, the Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering is listed as available for international eligibility review.

The stored admission requirements include:

- High-school graduation
- **English Studies 12** or equivalent: **73%**
- **Pre-Calculus 12** or an accepted BC/Yukon equivalent: **73%**
- **Chemistry 11**: **73%**
- **Physics 12**: **73%**
- One approved Grade 12 academic course: **73%**
- The **Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire**
- Competitive ranking by the program area

For international applicants specifically:

- The program has a positive international-eligibility listing.
- It is marked **eligible to apply for a post-graduation work permit**, but this does not guarantee approval.
- **Study-permit requirements are not published in the available Asteris data**, so they cannot be verified here.
- The equivalency of your prior education and the approved Grade 12 course may require institutional confirmation.

Check the [program details and international applicant information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/) and confirm current study-permit and credential-assessment requirements with the institution.
